title: Model a Business Entity
readerIntent: Add or extend a business entity using the supported schema framework.
priorKnowledge: Know the owning capability, users, lifecycle, and relationships.
owner: The business module that owns the entity
summary: Model business meaning first, declare only owned differences, and let Nodics create the runtime model and provider interaction.

sections.heading: Example: employee contact information
paragraphs: An Employee is profile-owned. Contact and Address records have their own fields and lifecycle and may be selected or created while editing an Employee. The employee schema declares governed references; the UI discovers metadata but the backend remains responsible for validation, authorization, and persistence.

sections.heading: Implementation path
items: Confirm an existing schema cannot be extended before adding a new one.
Choose a stable code, owner, identity, tenant scope, required fields, defaults, and lifecycle.
Declare relationships and access metadata using configuration values that layered projects can override.
Enable search, cache, versioning, publishing, or workflow only where required.
Use schema item models and services; never install or call a database client from the business module.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Create, read, update, search, deactivate, and delete behavior allowed by policy.
Required, optional, default, invalid type, length, range, enum, and immutable fields.
Existing-related-record selection and authorized nested creation.
Invalid, missing, cross-tenant, cross-enterprise, and cyclic relationships.
Provider-neutral contracts plus enabled cache, search, event, versioning, publishing, and workflow integration.
Regression of normal schema update and unrelated schemas.

sections.heading: Define business meaning first
items: Identify the owner and users.
Choose stable identity and safe description.
Decide whether Contact and Address are reusable associations or composed children.
Classify personal fields and retention.
List operations, search, import, export, and audit needs.
Describe tenant, enterprise, and employee ownership.

sections.heading: Design relationships
paragraphs: Decide whether contacts can be shared, whether one is primary, whether users may create them inline, and what occurs when an employee is deactivated or deleted.
Use supported relationship metadata. Do not store an unvalidated foreign identifier just to complete the first form.

sections.heading: Access and presentation metadata
items: Grant operations through configurable Profile-owned permission groups.
Define ownership for customer-owned and employee-administered records.
Expose only fields appropriate for list, detail, search, import, and export.
Provide friendly labels and display identity for BackOffice.
Keep localized presentation content in governed content or metadata.

sections.heading: Build through framework contracts
paragraphs: Let Nodics compose the schema and item model. Database services operate the selected provider; Profile never imports a database client directly.
If contact discovery needs external indexing, define the search model and use Search. The item model remains authoritative.

sections.heading: Run the example
items: Create an Employee with a valid Contact and Address.
Search and display it using friendly identity.
Add a second contact and choose a primary contact.
Update an address and verify audit and ownership.
Export and re-import representative data.
Use Schema Workbench to select or create permitted related records.

sections.heading: Negative and boundary tests
items: Missing, malformed, excessive-length, and duplicate values.
Nonexistent, unauthorized, or wrong-tenant relation.
Collection minimum, maximum, and duplicate entry.
Forbidden fields and operations.
Provider or index failure and partial nested creation.
Project extension absent and present.

sections.heading: Completion checklist
items: One owner and no parallel data authority.
Schema, models, persistence, search, API, and UI metadata agree.
Backend enforces security and tenant boundaries.
Migration, lifecycle, retention, and deletion are documented.
Beginner, business, developer, and operator guidance is current.
Generated artifacts and regression evidence pass.
